chapter: The Raeburn band: people and touring
title: Frankie Socolow, Hy Mandel and what made the band great
summary: He praises Socolow and says the band was great though some players were weak.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: What about some of the other people on the band. Frankie Socolow was on and off from day one almost.

That's the sweetheart of all times. That's the sweetest guy that was ever born, that ever lived; nicest person and a wonderful musician. He worked with me this past summer. I used him in my summer band and he left me the last week to go do the Jerry Lewis Telethon. He has nothing but compliments from me, as far as Frank Socolow is concerned. A wonderful
musician and a marvelous human being. A terrific guy.
That's one of the mysteries of the Boyd Raeburn Band.
Hy was a manager for a while, was he not?
Years later he became the manager.

I think the Raeburn Band, in the period '43/44 was probably the best band that I had ever heard or played with, the most interesting band; it was a marvelous band. The band played like everyone was born together, everybody was a twin, a part of each other, yet, if there were fourteen guys on that band, six of them I would say were top grade musicians, and four of them might have been the worst musicians that ever lived. Yet, together it was an unbelievably marvelous band, and that proved to me that a good man is not created by using the best person you could find on each chair. As long as people
could fill the demands of the chair, that's all you need to create a great band.

Hy Mandel is a rather bad saxophone player; I've always felt he was terrible, yet in that band he played his part, never got in the way, never interfered. He was right for the chair,for the time, for the music.
Was he a jazz player at all?
I've been asked about that many times, how could the band have been that great and had Hy Mandel playing an important chair. It was and he did.
